definitions.explanation: A flexible medical instrument with a small camera on the tip, inserted into the body (often through the mouth, nose, or anus) to examine the stomach, intestines, or other organs. By extension, the word is also used to refer to an endoscopic examination itself.

examples.japanese: {内視鏡|ないしきょう}{検査|けんさ}。
{明日|あした}は{胃|い}の{内視鏡|ないしきょう}{検査|けんさ}を{受|う}ける{予定|よてい}だ。
examples.english: Tomorrow I am scheduled to undergo a gastric endoscopy.

examples.japanese: {医師|いし}は{内視鏡|ないしきょう}を{使|つか}って{患部|かんぶ}を{確認|かくにん}し、{手術|しゅじゅつ}の{必要性|ひつようせい}を{判断|はんだん}した。
examples.english: The doctor used an endoscope to check the affected area and decided whether surgery was necessary.

notes:
Composed of {内|ない} (inside) and {視鏡|しきょう} (instrument for viewing). An everyday medical word in Japan because endoscopic cancer screenings (especially stomach and colon) are widely recommended. The associated examinations are called {胃|い}カメラ (lit. "stomach camera") and {大腸|だいちょう}カメラ (lit. "large intestine camera") in casual speech.

USAGE:
Usually appears in compounds with {検査|けんさ} (examination) or {手術|しゅじゅつ} (surgery): {内視鏡|ないしきょう}{検査|けんさ}, {内視鏡|ないしきょう}{手術|しゅじゅつ}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {内視鏡|ないしきょう}{検査|けんさ}: endoscopic examination
- {内視鏡|ないしきょう}{手術|しゅじゅつ}: endoscopic surgery
- {内視鏡|ないしきょう}を{入|い}れる: to insert an endoscope
- {胃|い}の{内視鏡|ないしきょう}: a gastric endoscopy

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {胃|い}カメラ: "stomach camera" — casual term for gastric endoscopy
- {大腸|だいちょう}カメラ: "colon camera" — casual term for colonoscopy
- {レントゲン}: X-ray
- エコー: ultrasound
- {CT検査|しーてぃーけんさ}: CT scan
